daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo Subianto marked two years in office with a record of eight cabinet reshuffles, raising questions about performance and stability. The administration has also faced scrutiny over governance structures, with the Presidential Advisory Council law challenged in the Constitutional Court over concerns that its 36-member structure constitutes wasteful spending. Meanwhile, mass demonstrations are planned for 20 October to voice public grievances at the two-year mark of the Prabowo-Gibran government.

  • PAN responded to surveys of Prabowo's government by stating that success should not be measured by numbers alone.
  • Another NasDem cadre has defected to PSI, marking continued inter-party movement.
  • The 26-member Presidential Advisory Council is being challenged as wasteful budget expenditure in a Constitutional Court case.
  • Police Metro Command called for orderly public demonstrations as activists prepared to rally.
  • The police prepared traffic diversions for demonstrations planned near the Presidential Palace and DPR building.
  • A Yogyakarta Sultan HB X questioned the system of channeling civil servant salaries through the Merah Putih cooperative.
  • AHY called for solidarity between politicians and academics.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Foreign Minister Nasir met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres to urge comprehensive UN reform, emphasizing that multilateralism is a necessity in the current global context. The visit, which included Guterres staying in Hambalang and visiting the Foreign Ministry, was described by the Foreign Minister as recognition of Indonesia's global role. Indonesia is seeking seats on the UN Security Council and WHO leadership to strengthen multilateral systems.

  • President Prabowo awarded 140 police officers who completed UN peacekeeping missions.
  • Indonesia pushed for OIC reform during a meeting in Baghdad.
  • Malaysia will send three aircraft to assist Indonesia with forest fire management.

Other

The Financial Services Authority (OJK) pledged support for financial stability and strict market reform amid ongoing market volatility, while an former minister alleged Singaporean interference behind MSCI's threat to downgrade Indonesian stocks. The Indonesia Stock Exchange announced it will change automatic rejection boundaries, allowing stocks priced at Rp 11-14 to fall to Rp 1, while 80 stocks face removal from the composite index calculation.

  • Investment reached Rp 3,923 trillion during Prabowo's first two years in office.
  • Bank Indonesia stepped up market intervention to shield the rupiah from further depreciation.
  • The government called for wider B50 biodiesel use and faster EV adoption in greater Jakarta.
  • Indonesia sanctioned 32 companies for forest fires as authorities intensified enforcement against environmental violations.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs restored 98 percent of worship sites damaged by disasters in Sumatra.
